what_was_requested: Test the Xbox One Game Activity entry point: From the dashboard, open the Guide, navigate to the selected game's Game Activity section, and verify that Achievements, Stats, and Go to official club destinations are accessible, each displaying the game name and relevant content. Return to the dashboard and confirm no error dialogs appear throughout the journey.
what_was_attempted:
A 41-step automated test sequence was executed:
1. Captured the initial dashboard state showing Minecraft Dungeons II as the focused game tile
2. Pressed Guide to open the Xbox Guide overlay
3. Navigated right through Guide sections to reach Game Activity (4 right presses required)
4. Navigated down to and opened Achievements, verified game name and achievement list with progress indicators
5. Returned to Game Activity via B button
6. Navigated down to and opened Stats, verified game name and statistics (time played: 7h 40m, ranking)
7. Returned to Game Activity via B button
8. Navigated down to and opened Go to official club, verified game name and club content with navigation tabs
9. Returned to dashboard via B button
10. Performed error checks at each major checkpoint (Achievements, Stats, official club) for error dialogs or unavailable-service messages
All steps completed successfully with screen changes confirmed via pixel delta analysis and OCR text verification.
verdict_statement: PASS. All five required success criteria were met with strong visual and OCR evidence. The test successfully demonstrated the complete Game Activity entry point workflow: Guide opened, Game Activity section reached, all three destinations (Achievements, Stats, official club) were accessible with game name and relevant content visible, and the dashboard was returned to without error dialogs.
strongest_evidence: Step 6 (Game Activity navigation): Screen delta of 5.481 confirms successful navigation to Game Activity. OCR clearly reads "Game activity" heading with all expected menu options visible: "Achievements", "Stats", "Go to official club", and game name "Minecraft Dungeons II". This single frame proves the core entry point is functional. Additionally, Step 10 (Achievements page): Screen delta of 7.189 with OCR reading "Achievements", "Dundecns Il" (game name), "20/1000" (progress), and achievement titles ("Ka-BOOM!", "Track Record", "Expert Explorer") confirms the destination pages display both game identity and content. Step 19 (Stats page): Screen delta of 4.975 with OCR reading "Stats", "Dundecns Il", "Time played", "7h 40m", "Rank 1 of 1 friend" confirms statistics content is visible. Step 28 (Official club page): Screen delta of 22.067 (largest change) with OCR reading "Minecraft Dungeons II @", "Welcome", "Feed", "Multiplayer", "Progress", "About this club", "Recent activity" confirms the official club page loaded with game identity and club-specific content.
rca_summary: No defects identified. The test executed flawlessly across all stages. The rig health was confirmed at test start (GIMX reachable, capture card with live signal). All 41 steps dispatched successfully. Screen transitions were verified via pixel delta analysis (threshold 0.5; all critical transitions exceeded this). OCR text recognition confirmed expected content at each checkpoint. Error pattern checks (for "Something went wrong", "unavailable", "error", "not available") returned no matches at Achievements, Stats, and official club checkpoints. The only minor observation is that Step 36 (final B press from dashboard) showed a screen delta of 0.147 (below threshold), but this is consistent with the dashboard already being visible—the frame was stable and showed the expected dashboard content with game tiles and store options.
recommended_next_action: No action required. The Game Activity entry point is working as designed. The test can be marked as passing and the scenario can be used as a baseline for regression testing. If future runs show deviations, compare against the frame artifacts and OCR logs from this run (stored in run-20261015-125710) to identify the specific point of failure.
